title: Always happy to bring this one back!! #danieldaylewis #theatre #shake...
transcript: As long as we're telling crazy Daniel Day Lewis stories, I just wanna remind everybody that in 1989, Daniel Day Lewis was playing Hamlet at the National Theatre in London, and one day, in the middle of a performance, he just walked off stage. And not only did he not finish the performance, not only did he not finish the run of that production of Hamlet, he has not performed on stage since to this day. He made a comment that people widely interpreted as him having seen his own father's ghost on stage that night, although he later clarified that he was being more metaphorical. He said, “I had a very vivid, almost hallucinatory moment in which I was engaged in a dialogue with my father. That wasn't the reason I had to leave the stage. I had to leave the stage because I was an empty vessel. I had nothing in me, nothing to say, nothing to give.” And it's fascinating that all of this grueling work that he's done to get inside the heads of these characters on film, none of them broke him the way that it broke him to try to get inside the headspace of this character that might have hit a little too close to home for him.
classificationReason: Historical anecdote about Daniel Day-Lewis walking off a 1989 National Theatre production of Hamlet. Not a review of any production on the list; the referenced Hamlet is a decades-old production entirely distinct from any listed title.
